_note: Written pages: the writing need (data/world/needs.json) is met by a scribe writing on a surface with ink, so scribes get demand from literate people's use of writing. One recipe for each surface; the household mix chooses among them.

written_page_papyrus.basis: per written page of a letter, account or copied text on papyrus
written_page_papyrus.yield_basis: A page takes one sheet of the writing surface and about a tenth of a gram of ink (see the ink figure below). A scribe in a book hand wrote a few pages a day: Lithub, 'Writing as spiritual practice: inside the world of medieval scribes' (https://lithub.com/writing-as-spiritual-practice-inside-the-world-of-medieval-scribes/, opened): 'A professional scribe could complete about three to four pages per day', which in an eight-hour day is two to 2.7 hours a page; taken here as three hours (a little slow, allowing for ruling and quill cutting); document hands were quicker. Services that turn materials into what households use are recipes on the trades that do the work, as the laid walls are. Pass 11 ink: onepenshow.com, ink economy (https://hn.jakechampion.name/reader/https://onepenshow.com/ink/economy, opened) measured fountain pens at 0.016 ml a page (fine nib), 0.04 (medium) and 0.05 (broad), from one test of three pens, so about 0.05 g a page at 1 g/ml; a folio in a dense book hand carries about twice a notebook page's writing (our assumption), so 0.1 g, taken as 0.0001 kg (was 0.0015 kg, fifteen times the sourced figure, so changed; a fountain pen is the modern analogue of a quill, and a quill's dip loss is not counted). Every figure in this row now has an opened source or one stated arithmetic step, confidence C.

Pass 11 ink: onepenshow.com, ink economy (https://hn.jakechampion.name/reader/https://onepenshow.com/ink/economy, opened) measured fountain pens at 0.016 ml a page (fine nib), 0.04 (medium) and 0.05 (broad), from one test of three pens, so about 0.05 g a page at 1 g/ml; a folio in a dense book hand carries about twice a notebook page's writing (our assumption), so 0.1 g, taken as 0.0001 kg (was 0.0015 kg, fifteen times the sourced figure, so changed; a fountain pen is the modern analogue of a quill, and a quill's dip loss is not counted). Paper sheet mass: papersizes.org, Weight of sheets (https://www.papersizes.org/weight-of-sheets.htm, opened) gives an A4 sheet at 80 gsm as 5 g, which is where the 0.005 kg comes from (modern machine paper as the analogue for a hand-made sheet). The desk and tools (timber, iron, carpenter hours, life) have no source found, so the row stays D.

capital.good: scribe's desk, ruling tools and ink-horn
capital.capital_basis: A scribe copies a page in the three hours the entry states, so one desk turns out about seven hundred pages in a working year; the desk and tools are a plank table, a stool and a few knives, and the item states them so the writing office is not treated as plant-free.
